column2: Yes, FALSE ECHO.
Excellent! I mean, ehr, alright. Thank you sir.
Hold on for a moment... what did you mean by excellent? Do you know what the main message is all about?
No sir, just overheard something.
What?
According to Naval rules and regulations, gossip is considered a felony under criminal code, section 2B.
True message, sir?
Yes it is. TRUE ECHO.
Thank you sir, I will be on my way then.
Much appreciated sir, I see that the message is authentic.
It is. Do you know what the main message is all about?
No clue sir.
Sir, it's ready?
Yes, one nice true message, authentic.
Are you sure?
What do you mean?
Maybe you've missed some detail or...
STASEC does not miss details.
Sorry sir, no disrespect meant.
Oh, authentic message. Captain will be pleased.
Say what?
I meant it's good that it's authentic, sir! One less chance for the damn Western Kingdom to infiltrate our communications! Sir!
Dismissed.
There you go sailor, TRUE ECHO.
Thank you sir. I am free to go?
Yes, go ahead.
Good day! I have a message that requires encoding, sir!
Very well, hand it over.
There you go sir. Hope everything is in order.
We shall see sailor, we shall see.
Yes?
I have a...a message that requires that thing you do with your device so that the enemy cannot read it.
You mean to encode it?
Yes, exactly. Sorry sir, I am a bit shaky after that depth charge attack.
No worries, give me the message.
Sir, message for encoding, here!
Easy now, keep your voice down a bit. Let me see.
Permission to speak sir.
Granted.
I have here a message that requires encoding procedure.
OK, give it to me, I need to check whether it's properly formatted.
Yes?
Message for encoding, sir! Written in plain text, sir!
It would be rather hard to encode an encoded message, don't you think?
I...I don't know, sir!
Sir, message is refused?
As you can see. Not following the official guidelines.
Which guidelines would that be sir?
I don't know sir, I am just a messenger. Permission to leave.
Granted.
Sir, message is rejected?
Yes, rejected.
But I don't understand why?
And I don't have time to explain every little detail. Anything else?
No sir, thank you sir!
Rejected message, sir?
Rejected. Next time ensure that all authorization prerequisites are fulfilled!
Yes sir, will do sir!
There you go, I had to reject it.
Why, something is not right?
Yes, some things are missing. You need to bring back properly formatted message.
Understood sir!
Sir, message is not authentic?
Message clearly violates procedures. Thus it cannot go any further.
Yes sir, thank you for your time.
All done sir?
Yes, take the message, you are free to go.
Thank you sir!
Thank you sir, much appreciated. And the original message?
Archived, as per regulations.
So I don't get it back?
Unless you are Naval or STASEC officer, nope.
Sir, it's done?
Yes, go ahead, take it to the radioman.
Yes sir, thank you sir!
There you go. All done.
Thank you...woah, I don't understand a thing now, how can they read it on shore?
A bit complicated to explain.
They will be able to read it, right?
Of course. Go ahead, you are dismissed.
Sir, I can take the message now?
Yes, approved for transmission.
Thank you sir, you are the best. Oppressia to Victory!
Sir, I have a message for decoding.
OK, give it to me.
Sir, I've been instructed to bring this message for decoding.
Let me see it. Who is it from? I don't see verification paper.
XO sent it, says that it's verified.
OK then, I will decode it in a minute.
We have a message to decode, sir!
Where from?
Ehr, radioman gave it to me, Political Officer told him to do so and ordered me to bring it to you.
No, I meant who is sending it...never mind, give me the message.
Sir, are you free at the moment?
Yes I am, what is it?
We have this message written in garbled text. They told me I need to bring it to you to decipher it.
Sure, give me the message.
Yes?
Hello...I mean, hello sir!
Hello.
Ah yes, there is a message that requires decoding, here it is sir.
Come in...at ease. How may I help you?
Sir, I have this message, SWO gave it to me. It requires proper decoding.
OK, let me see it.
Rejected, sir?
Yes. That's false communication right there.
OK sir, I will take it back. Thank you.
This is a false message, sir?
No, message is real - but definitely not for us.
So enemy intercept?
Likely. But we caught it on time.
Here, take this. It's a FALSE ECHO.
I don't understand, sir.
I am declaring this to be a false message, not to be taken into consideration.
Sir yes sir!
I am afraid that XO will be really, really mad with me.
Why?
He is the one who gave me this message for decoding.
It's not your fault that the message is not authentic.
False message sir?
Yes, rejected. Take it, you are dismissed.
Here, I am rejecting this message as being fake.
Do I need to sign something sir?
No need. Take this message back, you are free to go.
Sir, aye-aye sir.
All done sir?
Yes, message is properly decoded.
Thank you sir, I will bring it back where it belongs.
Here, message is decoded. I will keep the original.
Yes sir. Permission to ask why you are keeping the original, sir?
Standard procedure. I am checking the messages but some day someone will check my checks.
Message went through well, all clean, sir?
Yes, fortunately everything is in order.
Splendid, thank you sir.
Oh sir, that machine of yours is truly amazing.
Which one, the Obscura?
Yes, all the buttons and lamps. When you have time I'd love if you could show me how it looks inside.
We shall see, you need proper security clearance for that. Take the message, you are free to go.
All clear sir?
Yes, take the message, everything worked out well.
OK sir, I hope no one gets mad over this.
Sir, reporting for duty!
At ease. I brought you our new Daily Orders. Read carefully and try to avoid mistakes. Every letter you misspell or forget could mean the difference between life and death.
Let's see what this day brings.
I don't even know if it's morning or midnight.
At least there are no listening devices on a sub.
That headache will last a while.
I can sense XO in front of my cabin.
This will be a long day.
Rise and shine. I've got your Daily Orders. Did you hear that noise a couple of hours ago?
No sir, what happened?
Some trawler passed above us. Poor bastards, they scared us good.
New orders, stand up!
Read th Daily Orders with care and comply with the rules.
Yes sir!
(God knows you don't)
You said something?
No Sir!
New orders, sir?
Yes, I've got everything in your Daily Orders. Read, follow. Understood?
Yes sir!
Morning, lieutenant. Ready for this shift?
Yes sir, like Oppressian howitzer!
That's first time I hear something like that. Alright, here are the Daily Orders.
Verification message, sir!
Authentication?
Yes sir!
OK, give me the message.
Sir, a verification slip from the bridge. They told me not to fold it.
And yet you folded it.
Only where it was already folded, sir.
Put it here. I'll check the writing, not the creases.
Verification message for you, sir. My hands are clean this time.
This time?
Engine grease, sir. Nothing that concerns State Security.
Let me decide what concerns State Security. The paper, please.
Sir, I was on my way to the mess when they handed me this.
Your meal can wait while I authenticate it.
It has been waiting since the last watch, sir.
Then another minute won't surprise it.
New verification slip, sir. Straight from the radio watch.
Set it down where I can read it.
Sir, they said you would know what to do with this.
Who said that?
Everyone I asked on the way here, sir.
For once, everyone was right. Hand it over.
Permission to deliver a verification message, sir.
Granted. You don't need to stand quite so straight.
The passage is narrow, sir. It's mostly the door holding me up.
Then give me the slip before the door dismisses you.
Sir, the bridge wants this checked before anyone acts on it.
That's the correct order. Let me have it.
Sir, I've brought the verification slip. Nobody has read it aloud.
Was somebody planning to?
One of the men thought it would settle an argument, sir.
It will settle nothing until I've checked it.
A message for authentication, sir. Sorry about the wet sleeve.
Keep it away from the desk.
Of course, sir. The paper is dry.
Good. That is the part I need.
Sir, is this where I bring verification messages?
Yes. Have you been carrying that around looking for me?
Only one circuit of the boat, sir.
We have very few places to hide. Put it here.
Verification slip, sir. The officer on watch is waiting for your decision.
Then let's give him one. Pass it over.
Sir, I have been instructed to wait here while you check this.
You may wait without blocking the passage.
I was trying to keep out of everyone's way, sir.
Start by keeping out of mine. The slip goes on the desk.
Sir, this came down with instructions to hurry.
Did the instructions say to skip authentication?
No sir. Just to hurry.
Then we understand each other. Hand me the message.
Sir, may I ask something before I hand this over?
Briefly.
If the message is wrong, is the messenger responsible?
For delivering it intact, yes. For its authenticity, that's why you're here.
That is a relief, sir.
Keep it intact until it reaches the desk.
New verification message, sir. I came as soon as I was called.
All right, sailor. Let's see it.
Sir, I nearly took this back to the radio room by mistake.
What stopped you?
The chief asked why I was coming back with the same paper, sir.
A useful question. Put it here before he has to ask again.
Sir, the men are asking whether this means a change of orders.
The men can wait until we know the message is authentic.
That is what I told them, sir.
Then you have already delivered one correct message today.
Verification slip, sir. No additional instructions were given to me.
The slip will do. Thank you.
Sir, I've brought something for your stamp.
You've brought something for examination. The stamp comes after.
Yes sir. Poor choice of words.
An easy thing to correct. Give me the paper.
Sir, I hope this isn't a bad time. New verification message.
Messages rarely ask about the time. Let me have it.
Should I wait outside, sir?
Stay where you can hear me.
Sir, I was told to deliver this personally and return with your answer.
Who is expecting you back?
The officer on the bridge, sir. He was quite clear about returning.
Then don't wander off while I check it.
Verification message awaiting authentication, sir.
Bring it closer. I can't authenticate your announcement.
Sir, I kept this away from the galley, as instructed.
Were there instructions about the galley?
Standing instructions, sir. After the soup incident.
We don't need another incident. On the desk, please.
Sir, the XO sent me with a verification slip.
Any message from the XO himself?
Only that I should remember to call you sir, sir.
You seem to have remembered. The slip?
Sir, this needs checking. I haven't tried to make sense of it myself.
Good. Delivering it is enough for now.
Verification message, sir. I was going to knock, but the watch is changing.
The door doesn't become less solid when the watch changes.
No sir. May I come in?
You may. Give me the message.
Sir, I've been carrying this inside my jacket to protect it.
Protect it from what?
Mostly the elbows in the passage, sir.
A reasonable precaution. Let's have it before another elbow arrives.
Sir, I have a verification slip and a request.
The slip first. What is the request?
That I be allowed to finish my watch after this, sir.
Have you given me a reason to prevent that?
No sir. I would prefer to keep it that way.
Then hand over the slip and let me work.
Sir, this is the message I was sent to deliver. The instructions were very specific.
About the message or about me?
About not losing the message, sir.
A good beginning. Put it where neither of us can lose it.
Another verification message for your attention, sir.
There's room on the desk. Bring it in.
I thought you might be tired of seeing us, sir.
I get more concerned when the messages stop coming.
TRUE ECHO, sir? Then I can take it back?
Yes. Return it to the officer who sent you.
He'll be glad to see me arrive with an answer for once.
Make sure he sees the answer before he hears your commentary.
Authentic, sir. That's a weight off my mind.
You looked as though you were carrying more than paper.
